⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. This card is the parent. Its items are split into child cards once the maintainer answers.

**Verified on `origin/main`:** ADR-0084:47 requires "a permission **matrix** (roles × objects × CRUD + record scope)". `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` (around :961–985) only preserves `readScope` / `writeScope` and offers no control. No open or recent card tracks the gap (600 newest scanned; #26040 and #26056 are adjacent, not the same).

**Triage leaning on the four questions:**
1. **Item 1 → p1, `domain:ui`.** Two scope selects per object row, with the existing all-records exclusions (#16870) and an unlicensed-`hierarchySecurity` hint. Wire `PermissionPreview` read-only into the permission-set and position pages. About 2–3 dev-days.
2. **Item 5 (manual share UI): not this period.** Rule-based sharing works, and the server door exists. File it as a p3 card for later.
3. **Split the rest by landing site, not one card:**
   - #2: delegated-admin hints, `domain:ui` plus docs, p2.
   - #3: the server reason in the toast, `domain:ui`, p2.
   - #4: position drafts visible in the list, `domain:ui`, p2.
   - #6: hide or grey New without Create, `domain:ui`, p3.
   - #7: field-type Enter picks the current type, `domain:ui`, p3.
   - #8: the BU member title shows ids, `domain:server`, p3.
4. **Item 9 → framework, `domain:server`, p2, two cards.** 9a: the runtime save of an unlicensed hierarchy scope is silent where `defineStack` refuses it. 9b: explain names the wrong cause when the resolver is absent.
- **Also:** `hierarchySecurity` is WAIVED in `coverage.json` with no item. A `domain:devx` p2 card turns this run into checklist items.

Director seat, summon #51 continuation (ledger objectstack#12708). Presented to the maintainer in batch #396 as its one item, at the maintainer's word in the summon chat (「再和我讨论 #26059 清单确认」). Seat increment (re-verified on `origin/main` `cdd4eea9`; the test conclusions and the triage leanings 6414323834 are not restated):
- **Governing text holds.** ADR-0084:47 (Accepted): the Access pillar's editor is "a permission **matrix** (roles × objects × CRUD + record scope)". `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:961–975` only carries `readScope` / `writeScope` through a save (the #6605 repair) and offers no control. ADR-0090's ObjectUI landing list (`:642`) names "permission matrix gains OWD context per object row" and no scope column — the requirement sits in ADR-0084 and was never carried into 0090's list, as the card says. So item 1 is a declared-but-unbuilt editor, not a new capability: no ADR change, the contract already exists.
- **The pieces for item 1 exist.** `ObjectAccessScopeSchema` = `own | own_and_reports | unit | unit_and_below | org` (`permission.zod.ts:18`); the contradictory-pair refusal (#16870: View All / Modify All beside a depth) is on the BASE schema (`:632`), so the server already refuses what the UI must grey out; `previews/PermissionPreview.tsx:78–137` already renders both scopes (`SCOPE_ORDER`, `own+reports`, `unit+below`) and is not wired into the permission-set or position pages. `platform-capabilities.ts:224`: "ADR-0057 hierarchy scopes ship in the enterprise edition" — the source for the unlicensed hint.
- **Item 9a's premise is the card's, not re-verified:** `git grep -iE 'hierarchy.{0,40}(licen|entitl|enterprise)'` on `packages/{spec,core,plugins/plugin-security,objectql}/src` finds notes only, no compile-time refusal of an unlicensed hierarchy scope in `defineStack`; where that refusal lives (lint, or the cloud `security-enterprise` package) is for the dispatched dev to name before 9a is built as "make the runtime match the compile path".
- **Coverage:** cloud `docs/qa/platform-checklist/coverage.json:42` — `hierarchySecurity` WAIVED 2026-10-24, no item; this run is the material for the checklist card (`domain:devx`, in cloud, `cloud:checklist-author`).
- Adjacent cards #26040 (refused submit focuses the first invalid field) and #26056 (drafts-ledger read) are not this card's items; no duplicate found by the triage scan of the 600 newest.
- Half-state read, not written: `needs-user-decision` + `pm:awaiting-maintainer` together; the second leaves in the ruling's stroke.
- Facets block (the card carried none; written for the four questions as one decision):

- ② 实际业务拉动：客户管理员自建权限集时设不了组织范围、也看不到现状（实测 33/33 后端通过，唯独界面缺口）；问题 5 的手动共享服务端门已有、仅缺入口，零客户要求。
- ③ 防 AI 犯错：矩阵里的范围下拉按 #16870 置灰互斥项、未授权时提示，错配置在保存前被拒；9a/9b 让「声明了但不生效」在保存与 explain 上响亮。

## Item-by-item reading for the maintainer · director seat · 2026-10-26T12:26Z

Asked in the summon chat (「26059 要每个问题给我具体分析」). Every claim below was read on objectstack `origin/main` `cdd4eea9`; where the seat did not read a path line by line it says so. Each item: cause → where it lands → fix shape → size → grade the seat recommends.

**1. Record scope (readScope / writeScope) cannot be set or seen in the UI — p1, `domain:ui`, one card.** Cause: ADR-0084:47 declares the Access editor as "a permission matrix (roles × objects × CRUD + record scope)"; `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` models C/R/U/D/Tr/VA/MA (`:273–283`) and carries `readScope`/`writeScope` through a save untouched (`:961–975`, the #6605 repair) — the column was never built, and ADR-0090's ObjectUI list (`:642`) names OWD context, not scope. Lands in: `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` (two selects per object row, enum `ObjectAccessScopeSchema` `permission.zod.ts:18`), the permission-set and position pages (wire `previews/PermissionPreview.tsx:78–137`, which already renders both scopes, read-only), and the hint source `platform-capabilities.ts:224` ("hierarchy scopes ship in the enterprise edition"). Constraints already enforced server-side and only mirrored in the UI: View All beside a read depth and Modify All beside either depth are refused on the BASE schema (`permission.zod.ts:632`, #16870) — the selects grey out, they do not re-implement. Unlicensed `hierarchySecurity`: the three hierarchy values stay selectable with the hint "requires enterprise; otherwise owner-only" (the open runtime fails closed, `sharing-service.ts:377`). Size: ui M, 2–3 dev-days, no spec change, no ADR change.

**2. A delegated admin cannot enter Setup; the scope block gives no hint — p2, `domain:ui` + docs, one card.** Cause: `AdminScopeSchema` scopes WHAT may be assigned, not the doors the assigner needs: Setup entry is the capability `setup.access` (`capabilities.ts:49`), and choosing a person or unit needs `sys_user` / `sys_business_unit` / `sys_business_unit_member` read plus `sys_user_position` CRUD — the docs example lists the object grants (`delegated-administration.mdx:26–36`) but not `setup.access`. The UI block (`PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx:405–420`, `:677`) gates only the business-unit boundary (objectui#9464). Fix: in the block, a one-line checklist of the companion grants with a "grant these" action that adds them to the same permission set (one save, no new key), and the docs page gains `setup.access`. Not a server change: the server is right to refuse. Size: ui S + docs S.

**3. The refusal toast drops the server's reason — p2, two halves, `domain:server` first.** Cause, deliberate on the UI side: `isPermissionError` (`ui/packages/react/src/utils/error-message.ts:202`) treats every 403 / `PERMISSION_DENIED` as one class and the form renders it as the fixed line `form.noPermissionToSave` (`flowResponse.ts:336–369`, ruling objectstack#24914 B′) — a rule that exists so a denial never leaks why. The delegated-admin gate throws `PermissionDeniedError` for scope violations (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:403–503`) with reasons that describe the CALLER's own scope (`:1136–1179`, "outside the delegated subtree", "not in the scope's allowlist") — safe to show, but indistinguishable on the wire from a denial that must stay opaque. Fix shape: the gate answers its own code (e.g. `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, registered in the ADR-0112 ledger, status 403) and the UI renders that code's message while `PERMISSION_DENIED` keeps the fixed line. Not "show every 403 message": that reverses 24914 B′. Size: server S (code + ledger row + pins) → ui S.

**4. A new position saves as a draft the list does not show — p2, `domain:ui`, one card (confirm the premise first).** Reading: the editor writes `mode: 'draft'` only when the item sits under a `packageId` (`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:1104`, ADR-0086 P0/P2: authoring inside an installed package is a draft until publish), and `EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx:167` does the same; the Setup list reads published items. So the measured path is probably a position created inside a package's scope, and the gap is the list, not the save. Fix: the list shows the caller's drafts with an "unpublished" badge and a Publish action (the drafts ledger is the read #26056 is fixing for members; the position row rides that). Premise for the dev: reproduce which `packageId` the Setup "New" carried; if none, the draft write itself is the defect. Size: ui S.

**5. No end-user "share this record with…" entry — p3, `domain:ui`, filed for later, not this period.** Reading: the server door exists (`GET/POST /api/v1/data/:object/:id/shares`, `rest-route-ledger.ts:403–404`, family `record-shares`); the record page's Share item copies a link (`RecordDetailView.tsx:3436–3464`). Rule-based sharing through Setup works (card: 3/3). A dialog (user / team / position / business unit × read / edit) is a permanent surface with zero measured customer pull; the door being there makes this a gap card, not a capability card. Size when picked up: ui M.

**6. New shows for a user without Create — p3, `domain:ui`, one card (defect).** Reading: the list already gates New by `resolveAffordance('listNew')` → `crud.create` from the object's effective API operations AND `perms.can(object, 'create')` (`ObjectDataPage.tsx:503`, `affordanceGrants.ts:293–310`, objectstack#3391). The card still saw New for the auditor, so one of the two inputs answered true: the most likely is `can()` before `/me/permissions` is loaded (`resolveFieldAffordance` returns true when `!perms.isLoaded`, `:321`; whether `can` does the same was not read line by line) or View All cascading into the create verdict. The dev reproduces with the auditor set and pins the verdict. Size: ui S.

**7. Field-type search: Enter picks the current type — p3, `domain:ui`, one card.** Reading: `inspectors/FieldTypePicker.tsx:40–47` documents "Enter picks the highlighted type" and the list is a `cmdk` Command; the current type is rendered as the checked item, and with the current value kept at the top of the filtered list the highlight stays on it after typing. Fix: on a non-empty query, highlight the first MATCH (or drop the current type to its group) so Enter selects what the user typed. Size: ui S, one test.

**8. Business-unit member title shows raw ids — p3, `domain:server` (platform-objects), one card.** Cause is a formula, not the renderer: `sys-business-unit-member.object.ts:52–55` — `display_title` is `record.user_id + ' in ' + record.business_unit_id` and `titleFormat: '{user_id} in {business_unit_id}'` (`:38`) — so the title IS the ids by declaration. Fix: a title over the two lookups' display names; whether the formula language can read a lookup's name was not found in `formula/src/stdlib.ts` (no lookup-display helper located), so the dev names the mechanism (formula over related display names, or a stamped title kept by hook on both ids) before writing. Size: server S.

**9a. Runtime save of an unlicensed hierarchy scope is silent — p2, `domain:server`, one card (premise verified).** The compile path does refuse: `stack.zod.ts:4818–4845` `validateHierarchyScopeCapability` — a stack using `unit` / `unit_and_below` / `own_and_reports` without `requires: ['hierarchy-security']` errors with `STACK_HIERARCHY_SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` ("the open runtime would silently fail closed to owner-only; the metadata would lie, ADR-0049"). Its only reader is `stack.zod.ts`; the metadata `PUT` door runs no such check, so the same declaration is accepted at runtime with `_diagnostics.valid: true` and falls closed to owner-only — exactly the inert metadata ADR-0078 forbids. Fix: the runtime save door asks the kernel whether `hierarchy-security` is mounted and, when it is not, answers a diagnostic that names the enterprise requirement (refuse vs warn is the one choice for the maintainer; the seat reads ADR-0078 as refuse-on-publish, warn-on-draft). Size: server S–M. Lives in the framework: a self-hosted community runtime has the same silence; cloud's community mode is one host of it.

**9b. explain names the wrong cause when the resolver is absent — p2, `domain:server`, one card.** Reading: `explain-engine.ts:2040–2075` builds the depth record from `sharingFilter` / `depthAdmitsRow` / `sharingMatches`; when no hierarchy resolver is mounted the open sharing service answers owner-only (`sharing-service.ts:377–378`), so `sharingMatches === false` and the branch at `:2063` prints "outside the caller's 'unit_and_below' read depth" — true of the computation, false about the configuration. Fix: a resolver-absent branch ahead of it ("hierarchy resolver absent — requires enterprise; depth evaluated as 'own'"), one pinned explain cell. Size: server S. Pairs naturally with 9a in one dispatch.

**Checklist:** cloud `docs/qa/platform-checklist/coverage.json:42` holds `hierarchySecurity` WAIVED 2026-10-24 with no item; this run's 33 scenarios are the material. One `domain:devx` p2 card in cloud (`cloud:checklist-author`), after the maintainer's letters.

Recorded by the director seat (summon #51 continuation, `session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb`, ledger objectstack#12708; brief 6415795834, item-by-item reading 6415971852). The maintainer's two sentences, taken together with the seat's split proposal they answer: item 5 is out; the rest is split by landing site; whatever needs cloud access goes to the cloud lane.

**Q1 → 是.** Item 1 is the p1 child: the permission matrix gains a read-scope and a write-scope select per object row (`ObjectAccessScopeSchema`, `permission.zod.ts:18`), greyed by the #16870 pairs the BASE schema already refuses (`:632`), the three hierarchy values carrying the hint "requires enterprise; otherwise owner-only" (`platform-capabilities.ts:224`); `previews/PermissionPreview.tsx` wired read-only into the permission-set and position pages. No spec key, no ADR change (ADR-0084:47 already declares it).

**Q2 → 不做.** Item 5 (an end-user "share this record with…" dialog) is not filed and not built; rule-based sharing and the server door stay as they are. A future card needs a customer asking.

**Q3 → 分拆, by landing site — nine child cards, filed by the claiming seat of this parent (the `domain:ui` seat, with the triage seat first-touching each), every one carrying `Ruling-ref:` naming this comment and `Part of #26059`:**
1. ui p1 — item 1 as above.
2. server p2 — items 9a + 9b in one dispatch: the runtime metadata save door asks the kernel whether the hierarchy resolver is mounted (the open sharing service fails closed without it, `sharing-service.ts:377`) and answers a diagnostic naming the enterprise requirement when it is not — the compile path already refuses (`stack.zod.ts:4818–4845`, `STACK_HIERARCHY_SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`), so this makes the runtime path match it (ADR-0078 / ADR-0049); shape unless the maintainer says otherwise: refuse on publish, warn on a draft save. 9b: `explain-engine.ts:2040–2075` gains a resolver-absent branch ahead of the depth verdict ("hierarchy resolver absent — requires enterprise; depth evaluated as 'own'"). Framework code only: cloud mounts `SecurityEnterprisePlugin` by licence (`apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts:1333`, `:1597`) and changes nothing.
3. server p2 — item 3, server half: the delegated-admin gate (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:403–503`, reasons `:1136–1179`) answers its own code (e.g. `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, status 403, ADR-0112 ledger row), distinct from `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
4. ui p2 — item 3, ui half, `Blocked-by:` card 3: the toast renders that code's server message; `PERMISSION_DENIED` keeps `form.noPermissionToSave` (ruling 24914 B′ unchanged).
5. ui + docs p2 — item 2: the Delegated Admin Scope block lists the companion grants (`setup.access`, `sys_user` / `sys_business_unit` / `sys_business_unit_member` read, `sys_user_position` CRUD) with a one-click "grant these" into the same set; `delegated-administration.mdx` gains `setup.access`.
6. ui p2 — item 4: the metadata list shows the caller's drafts with an "unpublished" badge and a Publish action (beside #26056's drafts-ledger read); premise first: which `packageId` the Setup "New" carried (`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:1104`, ADR-0086 P0/P2) — a draft written with none is itself the defect.
7. ui p3 — item 6: New hidden or greyed without Create; reproduce with the auditor set and pin the `resolveAffordance('listNew')` verdict (`affordanceGrants.ts:293–310`; suspected `can()` before `/me/permissions` loads).
8. ui p3 — item 7: `FieldTypePicker` highlights the first match when a query is present, so Enter picks it.
9. server p3 — item 8: `sys_business_unit_member`'s title over the two lookups' display names instead of `record.user_id + ' in ' + record.business_unit_id` (`sys-business-unit-member.object.ts:38, :52–55`); the dev names the mechanism first.

**Q4 → 框架**, as card 2 above. **Cloud lane** (the maintainer's second sentence): what needs cloud access is the verification, not the code — one `domain:devx` p2 card in objectstack-ai/cloud (`cloud:checklist-author`): turn this run's 33 scenarios into `docs/qa/platform-checklist/` items, retire the `hierarchySecurity` WAIVED row (`coverage.json:42`), and re-run them on objectos-ee in both the licensed and the community posture as each child lands in a pin cloud carries. That card is the end-to-end re-verification of children 1–6; it carries `Blocked-by:` none (authoring the items starts now) and its run record waits on the pins.
